_meta.timingMethod: scaledStart/scaledDuration/scaledEnd = thoi gian THAT sau khi ap dung playbackRate 0.9 (giong doc cham hon 11%). Duration audio moi doan duoc do that (music-metadata) roi chia lai / 0.9, sau do ty le plannedDuration cua tung shot duoc scale de khop tong. Giua cac doan (section) co them 0.5s im lang de nguoi doc 'tho'. Moi shot co 1 transition rieng (shot.transition.type): CUT (cat cung, dung cho GAG/NUMBER - de cu punch-in/flash tu lam viec), WIPE (gat man hinh huong ngau nhien, dung cho BRIDGE/cau noi), DISSOLVE (tan mo, dung cho phan con lai va LUON dung o diem chuyen doan voi 20 frame). Khong con 1 cong thuc crossfade ap dung cho moi shot nhu ban truoc.
_meta.timingCaveat: Vi la linear scaling theo ty le chu khong phai do tung tu that trong audio, cac diem nhay cam (GAG punchline, SUBSCRIBE, COMMENT_BAIT, HERO) can nghe lai audio that va chinh tay lai scaledStart/scaledDuration cho khop chinh xac trong Remotion Studio, dac biet o Hook+Muc1 vi 2 doan nay bi lech gan 80% so uoc tinh ban dau.

_meta.editorialNote: beatRole = vai tro ke chuyen cua shot (suy tu so beat goc, xem ROLE_BY_BASE_BEAT trong script). motion = kieu chuyen dong camera theo vai tro (STATIC/PUNCH/PULL/DRIFT/SLOW), khong con la cong thuc chan/le. textOverlay = the trich dan nguon nghien cuu (7 shot) + nhan ten gen (3 shot) - chi dat o cho thong tin kho nghe ro bang tai.

shots.scriptText: Say hi, little guy.
Today your body is getting seven real upgrades,
...and every single one of them has actually happened to a real human being.
Seven documented abilities, one by one,
...and I've gone through the actual research behind every single one before giving them to you.
Save the last one for the end —
...it's so rare, scientists have only ever confirmed it in a small handful of people on the entire planet.
Number one: tetrachromacy.
You look at a sunset with a friend standing right next to you.
They see orange. You see about forty different shades of it, layered on top of each other.
A small percentage of women are estimated to carry the biological wiring for it — but only a handful of people have ever been confirmed to actually use the extra channel.
It comes from having four types of colour-sensing cells in your eye instead of the usual three.
(tiep - cham thu 4 nay vao)
A team at Newcastle University led by Dr. Gabriele Jordan tested a subject with this trait and found she could reliably tell apart colours the rest of us would swear were identical.
You're seeing roughly a hundred times more shades of colour than the person standing next to you.
But the extra channel only reaches full power in a brain that was raised paying close attention to colour — otherwise it mostly just sits there, unused.
So your eyes might already be ready. Your brain, not yet. There we go — one upgrade installed.
Let's fix the brain part next, with an ear that doesn't need to see.
Number two: human echolocation.
You walk into a pitch-black room, click your tongue twice,
...and you already know exactly where the wall is and where the open doorway is — without touching anything.
Only a few hundred people worldwide have trained this skill to a genuinely useful level.
Durham University neuroscientist Dr. Lore Thaler scanned the brains of expert clickers
...while they worked.
She found their visual cortex
...the part of the brain literally built for seeing
...lights up
(tiep - cham giua duong)
(bo sung can canh cham tin hieu)
shots.note: chen giua S27-S28 theo brief goc, trung moc voi S28 - can ra soat khi lap audio that

shots.scriptText: ...while they listen to the echoes bouncing back.
(khong loi rieng - shot phan ung hinh)
Your brain is repurposing sight itself to hear the shape of a room.
But it takes years of practice to get reliable, and one missed click near traffic is still a missed click.
Done — sound is now a second set of eyes.
Vision through sound is one thing. Holding your breath like a seal is a completely different upgrade.
Number three: the free-diver's spleen.
You take one single breath, dive sixty meters straight down,
...and stay under for minutes while spearfishing along the ocean floor.
This is just an ordinary day for the Bajau people of Southeast Asia, whose spleens run about fifty percent larger than average.
A 2018 study in the journal Cell by researcher Melissa Ilardo and her team
found a specific gene variant in the Bajau tied directly to spleen size.
(chuyen canh - so do torso, danh dau lach)
(minh hoa 'fifty percent larger' bang hinh)
(gag hinh long giua co che)
That organ stores oxygen-rich blood
the body releases the moment it needs it most, underwater.
(tiep - vien torso chuyen mau nhat)
(khong loi rieng - shot phan ung hinh)
Your body is carrying its own built-in oxygen tank.
But this trait took generations of an entire population living off the sea to show up — you can't will yourself a bigger spleen overnight.
One organ built for the ocean, installed.
An organ built for the ocean is impressive. A skeleton that survives a car crash is next level.
Number four: unbreakable bones.
You fall down an entire flight of stairs,
...and you just get back up and keep walking, without a single fracture.
This has only ever been confirmed running through one extended family in Connecticut.
A 2002 study in the New England Journal of Medicine
found a mutation in a gene called LRP5
that makes bone-building cells work overtime.
(pop-in - luoi xuong day them)
(pop-in - luoi gan kin dac)
(gag hinh long giua co che)
That mutation packs bone density far above
...what the rest of us are walking around with.
(khong loi rieng - shot phan ung hinh)
You can go ahead and test your own bone density right now, by tapping that subscribe button hard enough to actually feel it.
Your skeleton is basically running on an industrial upgrade.
But a few members of that same family also reported extra bone pressing against their jaw and skull — density came with a couple of side effects to manage.
Bones installed, and they are not breaking. Bones that won't break is great.
A body that never even feels a break is the next, riskier level.
Number five: congenital insensitivity to pain.
You grab a hot pan straight off the stove,
...or walk on a sprained ankle for a full day, and feel absolutely nothing at all.
Fewer than a few hundred cases have ever been documented worldwide.
Research on the condition points to mutations affecting a gene called NTRK1,
which normally helps build the nerve pathways
that carry pain signals up to the brain.
(pop-in - cham o tay)
(pop-in - cham giua duong)
Without that pathway,
the signal for pain simply never arrives.
(khong loi rieng - shot phan ung hinh)
Nothing physical can hurt you again.
But pain is a warning system.
Without it, injuries often go unnoticed until they're already serious — doctors have to check the body constantly instead.
Pain, switched off.
Feeling nothing is one extreme. Remembering everything is the exact opposite one.
Number six: superior autobiographical memory.
Someone names any random date from your childhood,
...and you can tell them exactly what you wore, what the weather was, and what you had for lunch that day.
Around a hundred people in the entire world have ever been confirmed to have it.
Neuroscientist James McGaugh and his team at UC Irvine
studied the first documented case
and found unusually enlarged brain regions
tied to memory and habit. (vung memory to)
(tiep - vung habit to)
(gag chu - "BRAIN: NEVER DELETES")
shots.note: ngoai le duy nhat cho phep chu trong khung hinh (dang gag chu lam punchline)

shots.scriptText: (tom tat co che, lien ket lai nhan vat)
(khong loi rieng - shot phan ung hinh)
Every single day of your life stays vivid, forever.
But that also means every embarrassing day, every painful day, never fades either.
Nothing gets the mercy of being forgotten.
A memory that never deletes, installed.
A perfect memory is rare enough on its own. What's coming last barely counts as human at all.
Number seven: myostatin-related muscle hypertrophy.
You're born already visibly muscular,
...and by your first birthday you can hold your own body weight straight out with both arms.
Doctors have only ever documented it in a tiny handful of people on record, anywhere in the world.
A 2004 study in the New England Journal of Medicine
found a mutation that disables myostatin
a protein whose entire job is to put a ceiling on how much muscle your body is allowed to build.
(gag - Lumen phan ung truoc so do minh vua ve)
Take the ceiling away, and the muscle just keeps building on its own. (tran nut vo)
(tiep - co bap phong vuot khoi khung cu)
(so sanh co bap thuong vs myostatin)
(khong loi rieng - shot phan ung hinh)
Roughly double the usual amount of muscle, from the day you're born.
But doctors still don't fully know what that extra strain does to the heart over an entire lifetime
...it's been tracked in far too few people to say for sure.
And that's the seventh and final upgrade, installed.
Say hello to the most upgraded human on the internet right now.
shots.note: shot tich luy bat buoc - gom du 7 dau tich cua ca 7 muc

shots.scriptText: (giu khoanh khac hero, can canh chi tiet hon)
If you could actually keep just one of these seven for real life, which one are you taking? Fight about it in the comments.
Personally I'm taking the unbreakable bones, purely so I can finally win an argument with a doorframe.
I'll be waiting for you in the next one.
